title: 2027 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition Goes Down the Nostalgia Rabbit Hole

body_markdown:
Volkswagen is bringing the Rabbit nameplate back to the United States on a limited-edition version of[the GTI](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-volkswagen-gti-and-golf-r-mea-culpas-and-missing-manuals/) . Unveiled at the 2026 Los Angeles auto show, the new 2027 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition stands out with an edition-specific shade of green, a selection of blacked-out exterior details borrowed from the Golf R, and a subtle, heritage-laced Rabbit emblem on the hatch.


The Rabbit Edition sits between the S and the SE model in the GTI range, and it was designed exclusively for the United States. It stands out from other GTI trims with black-finished Volkswagen emblems sourced from the Golf R Black Edition, a black grille, black mirror caps, and a black roof. The 19-inch wheels come from[the Golf R](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/review-2022-volkswagen-golf-r/) , and they’re finished in—you guessed it!—black.


The Dark Moss Green Metallic paint (pictured) is exclusive to the GTI Rabbit Edition, though buyers will have other colors to choose from. In our opinion, the coolest feature is the Rabbit emblem on the right side of the hatch. It’s a tribute to[the original Golf](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/your-handy-1974-84-volkswagen-golf-rabbit-mk1-buyers-guide/) , which was sold as the Rabbit in the United States and built in Pennsylvania. The fifth-generation Golf was also marketed as the Rabbit here.

Inside, the Rabbit features the same ArtVelours upholstery found in[the GTI Clubsport](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/first-look-the-new-volkswagen-golf-gti-clubsport-is-the-hottest-gti-to-date/) sold in Europe. The rest of the interior is standard GTI fare, including a digital instrument cluster, a 12.9-inch touchscreen for the infotainment system, and red accents.


Volkswagen didn’t make any mechanical modifications. Power for the GTI Rabbit Edition comes from a turbocharged, 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine rated at 241 horsepower and 273 pound-feet of torque. It spins the front wheels via a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission; The GTI hasn’t been available with a stick[since 2024](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/volkswagen-manual-transmission-for-gti-and-golf-r-gone-after-2024/) . The DCC adaptive damping system is standard.


Pricing for the 2027 Volkswagen GTI Rabbit Edition hasn’t been announced yet. For context, the base GTI S carries a base price of $34,905 while the SE starts at $39,095. It stands to reason that the Rabbit will slot between those two models. While it’s billed as a limited-edition model, Volkswagen hasn’t revealed how many examples will be sent to our shores for the 2027 model year.


Volkswagen will begin taking orders for the GTI Rabbit Edition during the second quarter of 2027. You’re not entirely out of luck if you’re in Canada: While the Rabbit will exclusively be sold in the United States, buyers in Canada will be able to configure the Autobahn trim in Dark Moss Green Metallic and with a new Black Edition Package that adds some of the blacked-out trim pieces.


This isn’t the first time Volkswagen has released a Rabbit Edition version of the GTI. Rewind to 2019:[The then-new GTI Rabbit Edition](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/2019-vw-rabbit-edition-gti-is-bittersweet/) was available in two edition-specific colors, had a 228-horsepower turbo-four, and wore the cool-looking Rabbit emblem.
